definition: GPT-5.3-Codex (Generative Pre-trained Transformer 5.3 Codex) is a large language model (LLM) announced and released by OpenAI on February 5, 2026.
details: It is made as a competitor to Claude's Opus 4.6, focusing on code generation, speed and the ability to search repositories, run terminal commands and at the same time, debug code. In technical benchmarks, it is reported that GPT-5.3 Codex is 25% faster than Opus 4.6. GPT-5.3 Codex is available in the Codex app and on the web; access via API is also planned. According to OpenAI, GPT-5.3-Codex is the company's "first model that was instrumental in creating itself." On February 12, 2026, GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark was released in a research preview, which is a smaller version of GPT-5.3-Codex which supports text-only input. As of February 2026, GPT-5.3-Codex is only available for ChatGPT Pro ($200/month) subscribers.

explainer.lead: GPT-5.3-Codex is an OpenAI language model built for programming work, from writing code to searching repositories and debugging through terminal commands. It is aimed at handling several parts of a coding task in one workflow rather than only suggesting snippets.

tiers.eli5: GPT-5.3-Codex is like a helper that can read through a big box of building instructions, write new instructions, and test whether the creation works. If something breaks, it can look for the problem and try a fix. It is made especially for helping people build computer programs.
tiers.practitioner: Use it through the Codex app or on the web for repository exploration, code generation, terminal execution, and debugging; API access is planned. As of February 2026, access requires a ChatGPT Pro subscription at $200 per month. Treat the reported 25% speed advantage over Claude Opus 4.6 as a benchmark result rather than a guarantee for every workload.
tiers.paperLevel: GPT-5.3-Codex is a large language model for code generation and repository-level programming tasks, with capabilities spanning repository search, terminal commands, and debugging. OpenAI reports that it is 25% faster than Claude Opus 4.6 on technical benchmarks. GPT-5.3-Codex-Spark is a smaller, text-only-input version released as a research preview on February 12, 2026.

flow: A programming request and repository provide the task and code context.
Repository search locates code relevant to the requested change.
The model generates code and can run terminal commands.
Debugging uses the resulting behavior to identify and correct problems.
For example, when asked to fix a failing login test, it can find the login code, modify it, run commands, and debug the failure.

explainer.whyItMatters: It combines several programming activities in a single model-driven workflow, including exploring a repository, writing code, running commands, and debugging. Its reported speed also makes responsiveness a central part of its design.
